document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Biodata (State 206975)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] Thumbnail sketches of Taliban officials, summarizing the emerging leadership weeks after the takeover of Kabul. Gives background on Mullah Omar, Rabbani, Ghaus, Hassan, Ehsanullah, Abbas, Wakil Ahmad and Yar Mohammad. Excised.

persons.name: Mullah Mohammad Omar
persons.role: Taliban leader, proclaimed Amir ul-Momineen (Leader of the Faithful); final voice of authority in the Taliban

mentions.quote: PROCLAIMED "AMIR UL-MOMINEEN" (LEADER OF THE FAITHFUL) BY A GATHERING OF AFGHAN ULEMA IN KANDAHAR IN APRIL
HOTAK BRANCH OF THE GHILZAI TRIBE
OMAR COMMANDED RESISTANCE EFFORTS IN KANDAHAR, ZABUL, HERAT, AND FARAH PROVINCES. DURING THE JIHAD, HE LOST ONE OF HIS EYES.

mentions.quote: MADRASA LOCATED IN HOME DISTRICT OF MAIWAND AND FUNDED BY KANDAHAR BUSINESSMAN HAJI BASHAR

mentions.quote: KANDAHARI MULLAHS FROM THE POPOLZATI TRIBE, YARANA AND BIRATHER HELPED OMAR STAGE THE UPRISING AGAINST KANDAHAR COMMANDERS

events.description: Taliban uprising against Kandahar commanders, leading to takeover of Kandahar
Omar proclaimed Amir ul-Momineen by Afghan ulema in Kandahar
Taliban capture western provinces from Ismail Khan
Yar Mohammad arrested by Masood while on negotiating delegation; released months later in JUI-organized exchange
Taliban takeover of Nangarhar, eastern provinces and Kabul
Omar proclaimed Amir ul-Momineen by a gathering of Afghan ulema.
Fall of the communist government; Omar begins teaching in a Maiwand madrasa funded by Haji Bashar.
Rabbani staged an unsuccessful uprising against Kandahar commanders.
Fall 1994 Taliban uprising against Kandahar commanders led to takeover of Kandahar.
Taliban captured western provinces from Ismail Khan.
Mullah Yar Mohammad became governor of Herat in fall 1995.
Yar Mohammad arrested by Masood in Kabul territory while on a negotiating delegation (spring 1995); released months later in a JUI-organized prisoner exchange.
Hassan left Kandahar governorship to become regional governor of Southern Zone; Abbas left mayoralty to become Attorney General.
Taliban took over Nangarhar, other eastern provinces and Kabul; Rabbani appointed Eastern Zone governor; Ehsanullah organized administration.
Consulate Peshawar cable 0926 on Taliban biodata sent; relayed by State on 4 Oct 1996.

key_claims: Mullah Omar was proclaimed Amir ul-Momineen in April 1996 and is the final voice of authority in a loosely organized Taliban hierarchy.
Omar relies on informal advisers Yarana and Birather, who hold no official position, and who helped stage the 1994 Kandahar uprising.
Most senior Taliban figures were former Hezb-i-Islami (Khalis) or Nabi Mohammadi mujahideen commanders from Kandahar and nearby areas.
A six-member interim 'National' Shura headed by Mullah Rabbani was formed after the September 1996 takeover of Kabul.
Taliban figures have links to Pakistani madrasas and the JUI, such as Samiulhaq's madrasa and Fazlur Rehman's prisoner exchange.
